text:
miriam: Heads up — seeing intermittent HTTP/2 stream resets for streaming calls when tokens rotate (dedicated customer env).

miriam: Root cause unclear, looks like ongoing stream gets a RST_STREAM with code CANCEL right after a token refresh completes.

kevin: ugh. repro on local? which client lib/version?

miriam: go client v0.12.3. repro in staging with low qps. Token rotation happens async via auth middleware that swaps Authorization header after a refresh.

sam: quick question — are you reusing the same http.Client/Transport across rotations?

miriam: yes, single shared http.Client for all requests.

kevin: can you paste the log around the reset? also try httptrace to see if connection is being reused or a new TCP connection is created.

miriam: logs below:
```
2026-02-11T16:02:11.123Z stream-start id=abc123 conn_id=10
2026-02-11T16:02:12.045Z rst-stream id=abc123 code=CANCEL conn_id=10 reason="auth refresh"
2026-02-11T16:02:12.046Z request-retry id=abc123 new_conn=11
```

sam: that "reason="auth refresh"" is from our client middleware or server? if client cancels the context that will cancel streams.

miriam: client middleware does a context cancel+retry to force new token on retry path if refresh races. it's probably too aggressive.

kevin: yeah, cancelling the request context will send RST_STREAM for that stream. For long-lived streaming RPCs you should avoid cancelling the parent request — instead patch Authorization header on the next request or use a per-request header injector that doesn't cancel active streams.

raj: quick workaround: set Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost higher and avoid creating new transports during token refreshs. also confirm Transport.DisableKeepAlives=false.

sam: also check req = req.WithContext(ctx) usage — if you reuse a context that gets cancelled on token refresh, it'll cancel the stream. Use a child context for timeouts only and keep token refresh separate.

miriam: patch in progress: switching to non-cancelling header swap and adding httptrace to assert conn reuse.

kevin: sample transport config that helped in similar cases:
```
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ExpectContinueTimeout: 1 * time.Second,
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

kevin: also use golang.org/x/net/http2.ConfigureTransport(tr) before client use if you need advanced http2 knobs.

ci-bot: linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/482 — miriam/token-refresh: avoid context cancellation for streaming

miriam: pushed fix, running soak test, will report back in ~1h :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for staging at 17:00 UTC

sam: if soak looks good, ping me and i'll review the PR.

miriam: thanks — will do.
